text:
maria: quick heads-up — I pushed a small experiment to split prefill vs decode queues and add a token-shaper that biases batch formation toward finishing prefill-heavy requests first. saw a weird 95th spike on small-context chat during the test run (results below).

maria: experiment details: spawn a separate queue for prefill tasks, token_budget_pre=48, token_budget_decode=16, and a soft deadline that favors moving small-prefills ahead of large-decode-only streams. also force kernel_selector to prefer small-TILE GEMM for <512 seq to avoid long fallback kernels.

kai: can you paste the exact config snippet you used?

maria: sure — config in case anyone wants to repro:

```yaml
batching:
  continuous:
    split_phase_queues: true
    prefill:
      token_budget: 48
      queue_priority: 12
    decode:
      token_budget: 16
      queue_priority: 8
kernel_selector_overrides:
  small_seq_max: 512
  prefer_kernel: "gemm_small_tiled"
  fallthrough_timeout_ms: 2
```

ben: did you also change KV eviction/warmup? prefill-heavy flows rely on KV being ready, otherwise we get decode stalls that look like perf regressions.

maria: Yes — set KV warmup concurrency for prefill queue to 4 and moved kv_preload=true for the first request in a session. That reduced wasted decode waits.

perf-bot: perf snapshot (canary v2 vs baseline):
- small-chat (avg ctx 64): p50 82ms -> 74ms, p95 420ms -> 250ms, p99 900ms -> 970ms (regression)
- long-stream (ctx 2048): p50 180ms -> 210ms (regression), p95 950ms -> 980ms
- throughput (tokens/s) +12% on short requests

alice: interesting — p95 improvement on short but p99 got worse and long-stream latencies regressed. flame graphs? maybe kernel fallthrough causes a long tail on some batches.

maria: I attached nvprof traces and the scheduling flame at https://internal.perf/trace/1793 — quick summary: a small fraction (~0.6%) of batches hit a kernel fallthrough path where the small GEMM didn't apply and we took a fallback that serialized across SMs, adding 600-800ms to those requests. these correlated with mixed prefill+decode batches where the batcher merged incompatible shapes.

kai: so split queues reduced some merge cases but our continuous batcher still tries to join across phase boundaries when token_budget left > 4. maybe lower the cross-phase join threshold.

ben: try lowering cross_phase_join_window_ms and also disallow cross-queue merging when kernel_selector would choose different kernels. quick patch suggestion:

```diff
- allow_cross_phase_join: true
+ allow_cross_phase_join: false_if_kernel_mismatch
+ cross_phase_join_window_ms: 1
```

maria: patched that locally — reran microbench on node-3. early numbers: small-chat p99 back to 880ms (down from 970), p95 steady at 240ms, long-stream p50 improved to 195ms. still seeing ~0.1% outliers that match rare KV eviction races.

alice: can we add a fast-path in the batcher to prefer forming all-small-prefill batches first up to token_budget_pre, and only then accept mixed batches? this could prioritize cheap kernels.

kai: agree. also consider a kernel_selector precompute per-queue: every queue advertises its preferred kernel profile and we reject merges if profiles differ. cheap check.

maria: added a quick heuristic: queue_profile = (max_seq, preferred_kernel_tag) and batcher rejects merges if preferred_kernel_tag mismatch. test run: p95 small-chat 230ms, p99 860ms, long-stream p95 960ms. throughput +10% overall.

deploy-bot: canary rollout: eng-runtime-canary-5 -> 20% traffic. watch for 99th regressions for 10min.

ben: action items:
- kai: add cross-phase join window config and make it 1ms default
- alice: prototype queue_profile tag propagation in batcher
- maria: hunt remaining 0.1% KV races, add jitter to eviction schedule
- perf team: validate on multi-tenant workload mix (50/50 small/long) and report p50/p95/p99

maria: one more note — if we over-aggressively prefer small kernels, we can cause starvation for long-decode streams under heavy load. we'll need a fairness throttle (token-credit refill for decode queue). added to TODO.

alice: ack — I'll sketch the fairness token-credit approach and post a follow-up with config and a sim.

maria: thanks all. patch/links: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/cont-batcher/compare/PR-824 and perf traces at https://internal.perf/trace/1793. will update once canary finishes. :rocket:"
